title: The Thornwall Dinner
sceneText:
After the main course one of the neighbouring landholders puts down his knife.

“That … predecessor of yours,” he says. “What actually happened there?”

Every movement at the table gets a little quieter. Everyone goes on eating, and the rhythm no longer matches.

Henk smiles. “Every man to his own road. Anybody who does this work long enough has a moment of wanting a different life.”

Marguerite says nothing. She is waiting for you to speak.

effects.logEntry: You said at the dinner that you were looking into Hartmann.

choices.resultText:
“I am looking into it.”

You know as soon as it is out that it was too soon.

Henk’s expression does not change. He is still smiling, and he sets his fork down half a beat slower than he did before.

“Looking into it,” he says. “Looking into what?”

You say there are places in the accounts that do not come out.

“The accounts.” He repeats it, and then turns to the neighbouring landholder. “There, you see — that is the good of a new man. What the old hands have grown used to, a new one sees is wrong at a glance.”

Somebody at the table agrees with him. And so the subject passes.

Marguerite has not spoken at all.

For the rest of the meal Henk talks to you twice about timber and once about the weather. He is extremely pleasant.

choices.text: I do not know. What I took over was the estate, not his affairs

effects.logEntry: You turned the subject of Hartmann away at the dinner.

choices.resultText:
“I do not know,” you say. “What I took over was the estate, not his affairs.”

The neighbouring landholder nods and says that is fair enough.

The talk moves on to this year’s prices.

You have lost nothing, and you have got nothing. You eat the rest of the meal in peace.

Marguerite looked at you once after you had finished speaking, and then bent to her soup.

You do not know what that look meant. You never work it out all evening.

choices.text: I arrived too late to meet him. You all knew him better than I — what sort of man was he?

effects.logEntry: You handed the subject of Hartmann back to the table.

choices.resultText:
Henk speaks first. He says Hartmann was “a man who took it all too seriously”, and laughs a little after saying it, as though there were something funny in the assessment.

The neighbouring landholder says his memory was frighteningly good — that he could recite an entry from three years back.

Marguerite does not join in. Only when the subject is nearly past does she say one thing.

“The last time he came to me was at the end of the summer.”

She does not say what he came for. Having said it she reaches for her water glass, and that movement ends the subject.
